items.title: A Decade in a Day: Synthesizing Agent-Native Interfaces from Human-Oriented Software Evolution
items.raw_content:
Authors: Alan Wu, Wei Tao, Yiwen Guo

Large language model agents are emerging as an important new class of users of desktop applications. However, existing desktop interfaces were designed for human end users or application developers, leaving agents to interpret visual controls or discover and compose low-level software operations. This mismatch can hinder even capable agents, yet it remains unclear what interface properties make desktop software easier for agents to use. To study this question, we treat software evolution as a natural source of interface variation and introduce DeskIF-Bench, a benchmark of 255 artifact-verified tasks across six desktop applications. By holding the task, agent, and verifier fixed while varying the software release, we measure how interface changes affect agent performance. Across two models and six applications, the newest release consistently outperforms the oldest. Trajectory analysis identifies three relevant interface properties: discoverability, granularity, and observability. Guided by these properties, we develop ANIS, a framework that synthesizes agent-native interfaces from the capabilities of installed applications. On an expanded evaluation of 368 tasks across eight applications, atomic interfaces improve success over native SDK use by 3.8 and 3.5 percentage points with DeepSeek V4 Flash and Claude Haiku 4.5, respectively, while reducing online token usage by approximately 73%. Goal-level commands further raise success to 74.5% and 67.4%, respectively.

items.title: LURE: a Phase-Labelled Synthetic Corpus of Online-Grooming Exchanges
items.raw_content:
Authors: Emanuele Florindi, Valentina Franzoni, Ludovico Guercio, Alfredo Milani, Mattia Polticchia

Phase-annotated conversational data is essential for studying the progression of online grooming of minors and for developing early warning tools. However, the only publicly available source (i.e., Perverted-Justice archive, which contains a subset coded using ChatCoder) is small, outdated, and frozen. We present a synthetic corpus of groomer-victim exchanges, generated using a retrieval-augmented pipeline running on institutional hardware. This pipeline uses an openly available, eight-billion-parameter, refusal-ablated language model. The corpus was created using the five stages of the responsible-generation protocol for synthetic datasets: ontology-driven design based on the ChatCoder luring-communication scheme (eight communicative tags mapped onto four grooming phases); multi-model prompt testing; human-in-the-loop supervision; semantic and feature-level validation; and modality-aware documentation. The released corpus contains 2,121 unique exchanges across seven tags and four phases, each accompanied by a Plutchik emotion field. Validation quantifies the integrity and lexical profile of the corpus, as well as the reproduction of real seed lines, in-domain label recoverability (tag accuracy: 0.85; phase accuracy: 0.93) and its transfer to real ChatCoder offender lines, which were coded automatically at the eight-tag level (31,640 lines) and by human coders at the three-construct level (10,876 posts). Accuracy was measured for lexical and sentence-embedding features, while a real-versus-synthetic discriminator was able to separate the two domains with 91% accuracy. The scope of the corpus includes controlled, phase-conditioned experimentation, pipeline development and augmentation alongside real data and awareness material. The corpus, its datasheet and the audit code are released with vetted access.

items.title: History Replays Itself: Unleashing Long-Context Capability in Linear Attention
items.raw_content:
Authors: Li Nanbo, Firas Laakom, Yilan Zhang, Piotr Piękos, Yimeng Chen et al.

Linear attention promises the efficiency needed for long-context language modelling, yet its fixed-size recurrent state must simultaneously support ongoing computation and preserve information from an ever-growing history. This coupling has reinforced a prevailing view that the state's memory capacity defines the model's long-context capability. We challenge this presumed ceiling: \emph{recurrent computation need not bear the full burden of long-term storage}. We introduce NoteBank, a sparse episodic memory that archives selected text before future queries are known, uses the backbone's native features for writing and addressing, and reads retrieved evidence through its native forward computation via replay. This \emph{training-free, plug-and-play} interface requires no external embedding model, separately trained retriever, or separate neural reader. At one million tokens, it raises Gated DeltaNet's mean accuracy across six RULER retrieval tasks from 1.7% to 70.3%, with no observed significant retrieval degradation from 4K to 1M tokens. This recovery adds $\leqslant$0.025% to analytical FLOPs, with persistent context storage approximately 1/2,600 that of a Transformer's full MHA KV cache at matched width, depth, and precision. Experiments extend from three 1.3B recurrent backbones to Mamba-2-8B and post-trained Qwen3.5-9B, demonstrating gains on LongBench v1/v2 and MemoryAgentBench. Together, these results show that sparse evidence storage and native replay can substantially expand the long-context capability of pretrained linear attention models while retaining the efficiency of recurrent computation.

items.title: LLM Value Functions for Credit Assignment in Agentic RL
items.raw_content:
Authors: Kaijie Zhu, Weixiang Yan, Omar Attia, Abbas Kazerouni, Alexander Toshev et al.

Reinforcement learning (RL) for large language model (LLM) agents remains challenging in long-horizon tasks with sparse outcome rewards, where assigning credit to individual actions is difficult. Methods such as GRPO assign the same trajectory-level advantage to all actions, while critic-based methods require learning an additional value function that can be costly and unstable. We introduce LLM Value Function RL (LVRL), which uses the pretrained knowledge and in-context learning ability of an LLM to estimate policy-aware state values without finetuning a separate critic. LVRL conditions the value model on group context and calibrates its predictions using known values at the initial and terminal states, enabling step-level credit assignment from estimated value differences. We further extend this idea to learning from an expert policy through on-policy distillation (OPD), introducing LLM Value Function OPD (LVOPD), which focuses teacher supervision on actions associated with decreases in estimated value. We evaluate our approach across diverse agentic benchmarks: AppWorld, BabyAI, and SWE-bench Verified. Across policy scales (4B to 32B), LVRL consistently and substantially outperforms both GRPO and PPO. On AppWorld and SWE-bench Verified, LVRL yields absolute improvements of up to 13.6 and 8.6 percentage points over GRPO. Notably, on tasks requiring extended exploration like BabyAI, LVRL bridges the gap from total failure to 75.0% success. Furthermore, LVOPD yields consistent improvements over standard distillation baselines on AppWorld. Finally, Monte-Carlo analysis confirms that our frozen critic accurately identifies semantic pitfalls and recoveries, proving that LVRL extracts robust, policy-aware step-level credit from sparse terminal outcomes.

items.title: SkillMarker: A KGW-Based Watermarking Method for Agent Skill Ownership Verification
items.raw_content:
Authors: Alan Tang, Lifeng Wang, Gang Wu, Tao Zhang, Yantao Jia et al.

Agent skills encode operational procedures and domain expertise as reusable knowledge assets, yet their distribution in plaintext exposes them to unauthorized copying and leakage. However, practical mechanisms for skill ownership verification and leakage tracing remain underdeveloped. Watermark embedding before distribution offers a potential solution, but structured, compact skill instructions impose stringent requirements for factual and procedural accuracy. To address these challenges, we introduce SkillMarker, a KGW-based watermarking method that jointly targets functionality preservation and strong watermark embedding. SkillMarker unifies quality-constrained rewriting with signal-oriented candidate search. The former separates essential knowledge from flexible expression to preserve instruction fidelity; the latter explores alternative expressions to obtain a stronger watermark signal under preservation constraints. We release an open-source toolkit that integrates watermark embedding, quality auditing, and detection to support the protection of agent skills. SkillMarker targets ownership verification and leakage tracing in distributed skill ecosystems, where content may be copied in whole or in part, or incorporated into other skills. Across four datasets, SkillMarker negligibly affects downstream task performance on average. In our copy-paste tests, window-based detection consistently identifies copied passages containing as few as 1,536 consecutive tokens. Even after merging with one or three background skills, SkillMarker retains watermark detection rates of 72.2--77.8\%.

items.title: SurgiCLAW: An Interpretable Atomic-Skill Agent for Precision Robotic Micromanipulation
items.raw_content:
Authors: Angen Ye, junjie xie, Yujia Song, Junkai Huang, Dapeng Zhang

Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and vision--language--action models have provided robots with new capabilities for long-horizon task understanding and planning. In surgical robotics, however, end-to-end prediction of low-level actions remains limited by insufficient precision, opaque decisions, and scarce data. This paper presents SurgiCLAW, a hierarchical skill-based framework for precision surgical manipulation. SurgiCLAW confines an MLLM to intraoperative visual understanding, structured explanation, and atomic surgical-skill selection, while delegating physical execution to verifiable deterministic control programs. For brain--machine-interface implantation, a representative high-precision surgical task, we construct a state-to-skill invocation dataset and expand it through visual and state perturbations. The model first learns structured skill invocation through supervised fine-tuning and is then optimized using three rewards for action correctness, operation prerequisites, and format validity, improving action selection, operational safety, and output parseability. We evaluate subtask success, offline model comparison, real-robot performance, and ablations. On a fixed test set, SurgiCLAW achieves 94.6% skill-selection accuracy and 93.0% macro-averaged F1 (Macro-F1). Across 50 closed-loop real-robot implantation trials, it achieves an 88.0% task success rate.

items.title: ADAPT: Audio-Depth Action Planning with Transition-Aware Rewards for Lights-Out Industrial Navigation
items.raw_content:
Authors: Wenjun Huang, Shenghao Fu, Yian Jin, Yang Ni, Yifan Li et al.

Vision-language-action models for embodied navigation typically rely on RGB observations, limiting their applicability in lights-out industrial environments where visible illumination may be unavailable. We study illumination-independent navigation using spatial audio for target localization and depth for obstacle-aware geometry. To support this setting, we introduce DarkNav-Bench, a benchmark with 24 industrial scenes and four progressively challenging acoustic conditions. We further propose ADAPT, an audio-depth action-planning framework equipped with spatial-audio perception and optimized for closed-loop navigation through reinforcement learning (RL). Our key RL contribution, transition-aware reward shaping (TARS), defines a pose-aware shortest-action potential over a position-heading graph. Unlike conventional geodesic-progress rewards, TARS accounts for both feasible movements and in-place rotations, providing action-consistent feedback for policy optimization. Experiments show that ADAPT consistently outperforms training-based navigation baselines and zero-shot multimodal models on both seen and unseen scenes. On unseen environments, it achieves 90.6% success under Clean conditions and retains 60.0% success under the most challenging Localized Noise setting. These results demonstrate the potential of spatial audio and depth as complementary modalities for reliable RGB-free navigation in lights-out industrial environments.

items.title: AutoSec-RAN: Specification-Grounded LLM Fine-Tuning for Automated Security Analysis of O-RAN
items.title_zh: AutoSec-RAN：基于规范的 LLM 微调，用于 O-RAN 自动化安全分析
items.raw_content: AutoSec-RAN fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct through two LoRA stages on 69 O-RAN, 3GPP and adjacent standards documents, then selectively adds RAG retrieval over the same index for security triage without raw packet access. On a 5G/O-RAN testbed with labeled fronthaul DDoS replay scenarios, it scored a mean of 0.713 across 313 items on a Gemma-4-31B judge, with weaker performance on the held-out attack-direction class.

items.title: Large language model-generated patterns for epidemiological modeling: a multi-benchmark evaluation framework
items.title_zh: LLM 生成的模式用于流行病学建模：多基准评估框架
items.raw_content: The study evaluates LLM-generated behavioral outputs for hepatitis C-related behaviors among people who inject drugs against literature, agent-based model and survey benchmarks. Across three LLMs, unconditional directional recovery was 46-68% for 28 literature-informed associations, versus 82-93% when the models were asked directly to classify them, indicating only partial alignment and a need for more systematic evaluation.

items.title: PopGen: Generating Semantically Diverse Populations for Zero-Shot Coordination
items.title_zh: PopGen：为零样本协作生成语义多样的智能体种群
items.raw_content: PopGen is a framework that uses LLMs to generate textual descriptions of distinct agent behaviors and then translates each into an executable code policy, creating semantically diverse populations for multi-agent reinforcement learning. Cooperators trained against these populations achieve robust zero-shot cooperation with unseen partners across four collaborative environments, and semantic diversity scales with population size.

items.title: Revocation Is Not Complete at Receipt: An Executable Outcome Contract for Distributed Agent-Tool Gateways
items.title_zh: 撤销在回执时并未完成：面向分布式智能体-工具网关的可执行结果契约
items.raw_content: The paper defines C0-C5, a bounded outcome contract for revocation in distributed agent-tool gateways, and implements it as a persistent monitor over a frozen gateway set. In an experiment using Keycloak 26.7, eight agent-tool gateways and 16 AWS hosts, receiver-selective non-delivery still admitted 112 of 225 calls and all 112 effects committed, which the authors cite as evidence that transport success is not proof of revocation completion.

items.title: onehumanbeing/esp32-iphone-agent
items.title_zh: esp32-iphone-agent：用 7 美元 ESP32 让 AI 操控真实 iPhone
items.raw_content: The project lets an AI model operate a real iPhone with a $7 ESP32, using AirPlay for vision and USB HID for input. It works with any OpenAI-compatible vision model and requires no Mac, developer account or jailbreak.

items.title: Dissipative Lagrangian Neural Networks for the Interpretable Modelling of Passive Mechanical Systems
items.title_zh: 耗散拉格朗日神经网络：被动机械系统的可解释建模
items.raw_content: The paper proposes the Dissipative Lagrangian Neural Network (dLNN), a continuous-time system identification method that learns conservative and dissipative dynamics separately, with a parametrization constrained to enforce passivity. It is validated on trajectory prediction for a chaotic double pendulum and inverse-dynamics modeling of a six-degree-of-freedom industrial robot, and a symbolic distillation procedure extracts closed-form models.

items.title: The tilde in your PATH may not be your HOME
items.title_zh: PATH 中的波浪号可能并非你的 HOME
items.raw_content: The author describes a warning from the nono agent sandboxing tool about a writable PATH entry under ~/.local/bin, and explores why a tilde in PATH may not refer to the user's home directory.
